exposure: gestational weight gain categories according to 2009 IOM guidelines (<28 pounds, 28-40 pounds, >40 pounds)
cohort: 21,674 underweight women in Missouri delivering liveborn, singleton, term infants in 2002-2008
finding: The study found that among underweight women, gaining more weight than the IOM recommendation was associated with higher risks for preeclampsia, cesarean delivery, LGA infants, and low Apgar scores, but lower risk for SGA infants, while gaining less than the recommendation was associated with higher risk for SGA infants but lower risk for preeclampsia and LGA infants.
mod_finding: Underweight women who gained more weight than the Institute of Medicine recommendations had higher odds of cesarean delivery.
